questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that the university had relevant courses for my education, and that the destination was interesting for me to visit. Norges miljø og vitenskapelige Universitet was told to take good care of international students, which was also important to me. Norway was also an ideal destination for me because they have amazing nature and there is no language barrier as a Dane.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed my semester abroad! Campus was beautiful, I lived with great people and we had many trips around Norway in the
weekends.The
only thing making it not a 10/10 was that I found the teachers to be less motivated than what I am used to here in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found the website and information about how to find housing a bit confusing, but there was a great help to get via mail. Information about possible courses was a bit confusing as well, as it was difficult to see what level the courses were on and the scheme for each course (for this information we could use TimeEdit but this was not communicated before we got to campus). Otherwise the university provided good information prior arrival!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a whole intoduction week with all information needed and good activities to bring us International students closer.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different dorm rooms close to campus. Where were many different buildings, new and old, with different amount of people living together.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a ordinary kitchen that we shared 7 people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That all the buildings are located in the same area, but the building are very different from each other. When I was applying I thought that only Pentagon was on campus but that is not the case. The old pentagon bullings are bit old and worn down, so if you prefer more modern and new housing, be aware of this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I ended up choosing courses I thought to be very relevant for me, and these were also confirmed by my home university. Very late in the process, the host university replied that I could not take these courses which was a bit frustrating.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received very good help when I called the host university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end it was very successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use TimeEdit to plan your schedule and call the host university if they are late with confirming your courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was lower than what I´m used to at KU.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit more interactive than at KU otherwise a bit the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: Global Environmental Changes, Global Food Systems and Food Security, Bioscience, Ethics and Environmental Philosophy, Forage and Seed Crops

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:

questions.answer: I went on more small trips than expected which of course let to some extra expenses on transport and staying.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Where were many different organization and associations that you could join! I for example joined a folk dance club every Wednesday and a Outdoor club who arranged many weekend trips. Many kinds of sport were also offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Joining a student organisations is a great way to meet people on campus and in my experience they are all very open and welcoming! Both the folk dance and the outdoor club were great!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend using the cabins of DNT (den norske turistforening) for nice and relatively cheap travel experiences in Norway. In general I would recommend people to take the train up north to the mountains and experience the beautiful nature!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as Denmark and Norway is quite similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the events on campus and join a student organisation.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language could sometimes be a challenge as some has difficulty understanding danish especially in bigger or louder groups.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People in Norway can be a bit hesitating to open up for exchange students if they are English talking. When understanding Norwegian it was definitely more easy to integrate.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living in the dorm rooms on campus - Pentagon, Pallisaden, Krona, Pomona or the other student housing close to campus. I also recommend students to explore more of Norway than just around Ås. Going North by train for a couple of hours will give amazing nature experiences and you can rent all kind of outdoor equipment on campus for free if you become a member of the outdoor club (Friluftslivet) which is definitely worth the small semester fee! Embrace the very active student environment on campus, join the events and meet other students! There are especially many opportunities to meet all the other internationals!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many opportunities to borrow outdoor equipment in Norway for free. Having a Norwegian phone number might be helpful as much is paid for through Vipps and if you want to make account for example for borrowing stuff you also need a norwegian phone number. However using a Norwegian phone company can be very expensive so maybe have a separate SIM card for the norwegian phone number.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other international students and being a part of that amazing community! And the nature experiences in Norway was also magnificent.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Starting a new everyday life somewhere new could be challenging, but as soon as I got close with my roommates, it became much easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going on exchange on NMBU!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
